A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SoccerReplay-1988 dataset and MatchVision model. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: V1 reports original event-classification, commentary-generation, and foul-recognition results, ablations in Tables 2–5, and training curves and qualitative examples in the appendix.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and additionally reports manual annotation verification in Section 3.3 and Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: The encoder architecture, supervised and contrastive objectives, hybrid training, downstream heads, and annotation prompt remain unchanged. Calling MatchVision a soccer-specific visual encoder revises its positioning, not its procedure.

E1.justification: Both use SoccerReplay-1988, curated SoccerNet-v2 and MatchTime, and MVFoul for the same three tasks. The annotation audit and additional foul comparisons do not establish new dataset or task coverage; proposed future tasks remain unevaluated.

E2.justification: V3 adds a supplementary foul-recognition comparison in Appendix D.2, Table 10, including challenge entries zyz, PD_PS_GSN, Redsox, and xiao_he_shang. Comparator membership in the existing Tables 2–3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: V3 introduces a manual annotation-validation procedure using a random 2% data sample. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, clip sampling, model configurations, and training budgets remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish that these experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 3.3 and Appendix A.3 add an annotation-quality check reporting 98% manual verification accuracy. Existing training-strategy and dataset ablations, convergence plots, and qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added annotation audit reports point accuracy without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark and ablation scores are unchanged. V3 adds the 98% annotation-verification result and challenge scores in Table 10, including Redsox foul accuracy of 0.60 alongside MatchVision's retained 0.44. These are additional results, not cross-version performance gains.

T1.justification: The formal problem formulation, embedding and aggregation equations, and training objectives remain equivalent. Neither version contains additional theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace the claim of the first soccer visual-language foundation model with a soccer-specific visual encoder. This narrows the model's novelty and scope claim while retaining the dataset, multitask framework, and performance contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly identifies European-league concentration and computational and annotation constraints as limitations. It proposes broader data collection and replaces game-state reconstruction with dense video captioning among future tasks. Existing interpretations of the main experiments remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: V3 explicitly states that videos and annotations are available for non-commercial use. Appendix A.3 newly documents manual prompt refinement and exclusion of nonvisual statistics-and-summary commentary. These are additional disclosures; an actual change to the underlying filtering procedure is not established.

R1.justification: Related work adds references including SoccerNet 2024 challenges, Video-XL, MLVU, and EIKA, and removes the player-and-ball-detection citation. Model positioning becomes more restrained, while the overall argument for unified soccer understanding remains.

P1.justification: V3 makes local rewrites and terminology refinements throughout the paper, adds acknowledgments, and inserts Appendix D.2 for quantitative comparisons, moving the existing qualitative subsection to D.3. The overall section structure and narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V3 adds Table 10, moves Figure 3 from page 5 to page 4, relocates Table 5 within page 8, and reduces Figure 6's displayed size. Captions and surrounding layouts change, while all nine existing figures retain their underlying content.

improvement.justification: The annotation audit, additional challenge comparisons, narrower model claim, and explicit dataset limitations improve support and transparency. Gains are limited: the core experiments remain unchanged, audit details are sparse, and the abstract still claims state-of-the-art performance on every task despite the stronger foul-class results reported for competitors in Table 10.
